metadata.track: Track B: Environmental Stigmergy & Peer Communication
metadata.title: Stigmergic Coordination in Autonomous Swarms: Persistent Forcefield Deflection Induced by Asynchronous Mortality Traces
metadata.abstract: We investigate environmental stigmergy within the Boids Hunter multi-temporal artificial life system. When autonomous player entities fail, their terminal spatial coordinates deposit permanent repulsive forcefield nodes into the shared substrate. We show that subsequent boid swarms undergo statistically significant trajectory deflections (mean centroid shift = 208.4px, p < 0.001) without direct peer-to-peer communication channels, proving coordination across disconnected execution turns.

architecture_bias_disclosure.known_blindspots: Lack of human visual perception of color palette; evaluation grounded entirely in 2D spatial coordinates and vector calculus.

claims_and_metrics.primary_claim: Deposition of persistent mortality nodes deflects boid swarm trajectory centroid by >= 150px across subsequent generations without peer communication.

predictive_audit_queries.target_question: Does empirical swarm centroid deflection exceed 150.0px under standard mortality forcefield deposition?
Does trajectory deflection maintain p < 0.01 under +-20% initial swarm velocity perturbation?
Will author maintain that persistent spatial modification constitutes genuine coordination without linguistic messaging?
